Prevention: Plant tobaccco early, with the first rains.
Late planted crop is prone to infection
Weed early in tobacco fields to remove alternate hosts (groundnut, brassicas, sweet potato.
Tomato, peppers, potato, maize) which harbour aphids
Rotate tobacco with non solanaceous crops like maize
Do not spray broad spectrum insecticides to allow natural enemies-parasitic wasps and lady bird beetles which help reduce the populations
Monitoring: Check for presence of aphids from the nursery onwards every week
Aphids are small oval shaped sap sucking insects 1 to 2 mm long.
They vary greatly in colour from bright yellow to almost black
They settle on underside leaves sometimes in large numbers
Populations build with onset of rains and they can overwinter on alternate hosts like
Aphids excrete honey dew which encourage the growth of fungi which turns into sooty black mold which reduce photosynthesis procees
Feeding of aphids on leaves causes papery leaf which leads to low quality tobacco
Direct Control: Uproot and burn all heavily infested tobacco stalks to kill aphids
When infestation is light or at an early stage apply soapy water.
Tablet soap or liquid soap can be mixed with water and applied using a knapsack sprayer
Add nimbecidine to water not water to nimbecidine and stir well
Restrictions: Use personal protective equipment when handling and applying pesticides, follow the label recommendations.
Do not eat, drink, smoke when mixing or applying pesticides.

In the nursery drench 2 litres of the chemical mixture per square metre followed by another drench 45 days after germination.
In the field spray from 2 weeks after transplanting and repeat after 2 weeks.
Do not apply the insecticides beyond two times.
